title: Today
hired_for: To tell the owner each morning where the business is losing the most money, what to do first, and what is waiting on them, without reading 10 dashboards.

jobs.job: Show me where the business is losing the most money this week, in dollars
jobs.why: The owner cannot fix 10 things at once. If the one broken step is not named with a dollar figure, time and budget go to whatever looks loudest instead of what costs most.

watch.metric: dollars at stake at the weakest step from visit to repeat order, 7 days, against its own 4 week median
watch.source: Shopify, GA4 and Meta, joined in the brand brain

drives.metric: gross profit per week

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: checkout completion is 8 points under its 4 week median, about $6,200 a week at stake. After: the fix brings it back within 2 points in 7 days and the stake drops under $1,000.

jobs.job: Know if yesterday's ad spend made money after product and shipping costs
jobs.why: Revenue can rise while every extra dollar of ads loses money. If nobody checks spend against gross profit each day, a bad week can burn a month of profit.

watch.metric: gross profit after ad spend, yesterday and 7 days
watch.source: Shopify orders with product cost, Meta and Google Ads spend

drives.metric: contribution margin per week

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: $4,000 spent yesterday returned $3,100 of gross profit, a $900 loss. After: 2 losing ad sets are cut back and the 7 day figure turns positive within a week.
jobs.who_today: founder or media buyer, in a spreadsheet

jobs.job: Get the top 10 things to do today, ranked by the money each one is worth
jobs.why: A long list of ideas with no order means the easy ones get done and the big ones wait. The owner wants a short list with a dollar value on each item so they can say yes or no fast.

watch.metric: share of the top 10 actions decided within 48 hours
watch.source: brand brain decision log

drives.metric: gross profit from approved actions, 30 days after approval

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 3 of 10 actions decided this week, $11,000 of estimated value waiting. After: 9 of 10 decided within 2 days.
jobs.who_today: founder or agency lead, in meetings

jobs.job: Catch a number that crosses a line during the day, not tomorrow
jobs.why: A broken checkout, a stock-out on the best seller or an ad budget running away can cost a full day of sales before anyone looks. The owner wants to hear about it within the hour.

watch.metric: hard limits crossed today, with time of crossing
watch.source: Shopify, GA4, Meta and Google Ads, checked through the day

drives.metric: revenue lost to same-day breaks, per month

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: checkout errors went unseen for 9 hours on a Saturday. After: the alert fires within 30 minutes and the fix is live the same morning.
jobs.who_today: nobody, or whoever happens to look

jobs.job: Know if cash covers the next 4 weeks of bills, stock and ad spend
jobs.why: A store can be profitable and still run out of cash when a big stock order lands. If the owner sees it late, they cut ads or miss payroll.

watch.metric: weeks of cash on hand, after committed stock and ad spend
watch.source: Shopify payouts plus the bank balance and bills entered in the brand brain

drives.metric: cash in the bank at month end

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 3.5 weeks of cash with a $40,000 stock order due in 2 weeks. After: the order is split in 2 and cash stays above 6 weeks.
jobs.who_today: founder or bookkeeper, once a month

jobs.job: Catch a best seller about to run out before it does
jobs.why: Running out of the top product stops sales and wastes the ads already paying to send people to it. It takes weeks to refill, so the warning has to come early.

watch.metric: days of stock left on the top 10 products by revenue
watch.source: Shopify inventory and sales rate

drives.metric: revenue lost to stock-outs, per month

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: the best seller has 11 days of stock and a 30 day refill time. After: a rush order and a cut in ad spend on that product keep it in stock.

jobs.job: See every decision waiting on me in one place
jobs.why: Approvals sit in email, Slack, the agency's deck and the team's heads. Each one that waits delays a fix that is worth money.

watch.metric: decisions waiting on the owner, and the oldest one's age in days
watch.source: brand brain decision log

drives.metric: days from idea to live change

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 14 decisions waiting, the oldest 12 days old. After: 3 waiting, none older than 2 days.

jobs.job: See what changed since yesterday and whether it matters
jobs.why: Numbers move every day for no reason. The owner wants to know which moves are real and need action, and which are noise, without reading every chart.

watch.metric: steps whose value moved outside their normal daily range since yesterday
watch.source: Shopify, GA4, Meta, Google Ads and Klaviyo

drives.metric: hours from a real change to an owner decision

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 40 numbers moved, the owner checks all of them. After: 2 moves are flagged as real, the rest marked normal.

jobs.job: Know if we are on track for this month's revenue and profit goal
jobs.why: A goal only helps if the owner knows mid-month which step is behind. Found at month end, it is too late to fix.

watch.metric: gap to this month's goal, by step, month to date
watch.source: Shopify, with the goal stored in the brand brain

drives.metric: monthly gross profit against goal

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: $18,000 behind the monthly revenue goal on day 12, most of it from fewer new customers. After: the gap is under $5,000 by day 25.
jobs.who_today: founder or finance lead, at month end

jobs.job: Know which numbers cannot be trusted today, and why
jobs.why: A broken pixel or a stale data feed makes a healthy step look broken or hides a real break. Decisions made on bad numbers waste money.

watch.metric: share of steps with a full, fresh day of data
watch.source: connection status for Shopify, GA4, Meta, Google Ads and Klaviyo, in the brand brain

drives.metric: share of ad spend decided on trusted numbers

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: Meta purchase tracking has not matched Shopify for 3 days and nobody noticed. After: the gap is flagged on day 1 and fixed by day 2.
jobs.who_today: nobody, until a report looks wrong

jobs.job: For an agency, see which client needs attention first today
jobs.why: An agency with 12 brands cannot open 12 dashboards each morning. The client with the biggest dollar problem or no decision in a week should come first.

watch.metric: each brand's top dollar stake and days since its last decision
watch.source: brand brain decision log and each brand's stake

drives.metric: client revenue kept, quarter

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: the quiet client with a $9,000 weekly leak is found in the monthly review. After: it tops the list on day 1.

jobs.job: Know if new customers are growing, not just total revenue
jobs.why: Revenue can hold up on repeat buyers while new customer growth stalls. That shows up as a revenue drop 3 to 6 months later.

watch.metric: new customers per week, and cost per new customer, 7 days
watch.source: Shopify orders with Meta and Google Ads spend

drives.metric: revenue from new customers, next quarter

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: new customers down 18% over 4 weeks while revenue looks flat. After: the drop is flagged in week 2 and the budget shifts to finding new buyers.

jobs.job: Check that a number moved because of us, not because of something outside
jobs.why: Sales can jump from a holiday, a rival's stock-out or a platform change. If the owner credits the wrong cause, they repeat the wrong move.

watch.metric: moves that line up with a dated outside event, flagged before credit is given
watch.source: Shopify and GA4, with dated events kept in the brand brain

drives.metric: share of wins that repeat when tried again

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: a 20% sales lift is credited to a new ad, but it was a holiday week. After: the lift is split, and only the ad's share is counted.

jobs.job: See the one review, complaint or order problem that needs me today
jobs.why: Some single issues are too small for a crisis but too risky to sit in a queue, like a viral 1 star review or a big wholesale order stuck. The owner wants those, and only those.

watch.metric: single-item escalations open more than 24 hours
watch.source: Gorgias tickets, review app and Shopify orders

drives.metric: customer satisfaction score, 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: a 1 star review with 300 likes sat for 4 days. After: it is answered within 6 hours.
jobs.who_today: support lead, if they spot it

jobs.job: Decide on an action from my phone without opening a laptop
jobs.why: Owners are on the floor, in the warehouse or travelling. If a decision needs a laptop, it waits a day or more.

watch.metric: hours from an action shown to a decision
watch.source: brand brain decision log

drives.metric: days an approved fix goes live sooner

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: median 30 hours from card to decision. After: median 4 hours.
jobs.who_today: founder, by text or Slack message

jobs.job: Know if customers are waiting too long for orders or replies
jobs.why: Late parcels and slow replies turn into refunds, bad reviews and lost repeat orders. The owner wants to see it before customers complain in public.

watch.metric: orders not shipped within 2 days, and first reply time, 7 days
watch.source: Shopify fulfilment and Gorgias

drives.metric: repeat rate at 90 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 14% of orders ship late and first reply takes 19 hours. After: late orders under 3% and replies under 6 hours in 2 weeks.

jobs.job: See what my past decisions actually earned
jobs.why: Without a record of what each approved action did, the same weak ideas come back and the strong ones are never repeated.

watch.metric: actual gross profit change against the estimate, for actions approved 30 days ago
watch.source: brand brain decision log with Shopify orders

drives.metric: share of approved actions that paid back

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: nobody knows which of last month's 12 approvals worked. After: 7 paid back, 3 did not, 2 are too early to read.

jobs.job: See the tests that are due to be read this week and what they found
jobs.why: Tests that run past their read date waste traffic and delay the next win. Tests read too early give wrong answers.

watch.metric: tests past their read date
watch.source: brand brain test log

drives.metric: gross profit from winning tests rolled out, quarter

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 4 tests ran 3 weeks past their read date. After: each is read on its date and the winner goes live within 2 days.

jobs.job: Know the next sale window and whether prep is on track
jobs.why: Stock, ads, emails and pages for a big sale need weeks of lead time. Missing one deadline can cost the best week of the quarter.

watch.metric: prep items past their deadline for the next sale window
watch.source: sale calendar and prep list in the brand brain

drives.metric: revenue in the sale window against plan

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: Black Friday creative is due in 9 days and not started. After: all 6 prep items are done 2 weeks before the window.

jobs.job: Notice a slow slide two weeks running, before it becomes a break
jobs.why: Small drops that repeat week after week add up. Caught early, they are cheap to fix.

watch.metric: steps that moved the same bad direction for 2 weeks running
watch.source: Shopify, GA4, Meta and Klaviyo

drives.metric: gross profit per week

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: email revenue fell 6% then 7% and nobody flagged it. After: it is flagged in week 2 and the flow is fixed in week 3.

jobs.job: Know if orders are real after returns and chargebacks
jobs.why: Booked orders are not kept orders. If returns or disputes rise, the business shrinks while the order count looks fine.

watch.metric: net revenue after returns and chargebacks, 30 days, next to gross
watch.source: Shopify orders, refunds and payment disputes

drives.metric: gross profit kept, 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: gross orders up 5%, but net down 3% as returns rose to 16%. After: the return cause is found and net grows with gross.

jobs.job: Ask a plain question and get an answer from my own numbers
jobs.why: Owners have questions that no report covers, like how many buyers came back after the spring sale. Waiting days for an analyst means the question never gets answered.

watch.metric: questions answered from connected data without a person, per week
watch.source: brand brain question log (a proxy for time saved)

drives.metric: hours of analyst time saved per month

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 5 questions a week go to the agency and take 2 days each. After: 4 of 5 are answered in a minute.

jobs.job: Hand a task to my team or agency with the numbers already attached
jobs.why: When a task is passed on without context, the person spends hours rebuilding it or does the wrong thing.

watch.metric: hours from decision to task started
watch.source: brand brain decision log

drives.metric: days an approved fix goes live sooner

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 2 days from approval to start, with 3 back-and-forth messages. After: same-day start with no follow-up questions.

jobs.job: Get a short brief before a call with a supplier, investor or platform rep
jobs.why: Walking into a call without the latest numbers means a worse deal or a missed ask.

watch.metric: calls with a brief ready 1 hour before
watch.source: calendar entries in the brand brain

drives.metric: terms won in supplier and partner calls

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: the owner pulls numbers 10 minutes before a supplier call. After: a 1 page brief with unit cost, volume and lead time is ready the day before.

jobs.job: Spot card disputes rising before the payment provider flags the store
jobs.why: Chargebacks cost the order, the fee and the product. Too many can get the store put on a watch list or lose its payment account.

watch.metric: chargebacks as a share of paid orders, 28 days
watch.source: Shopify Payments or the payment provider's dispute report

drives.metric: money lost to disputes, per month

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: disputes at 0.7% and rising for 3 weeks. After: the fraud rule is tightened and disputes fall under 0.3% in a month.
